item.name: API tokens
Create an API token (the token is returned once)

request.name: Create an API token (the token is returned once)

description.content: Creates an API token for the calling member in a workspace and returns the secret exactly once in the token field. Copy it immediately, it cannot be read again and a lost token must be revoked and recreated. A token can only narrow what its member may do. permissions defaults to all of the member's own permissions when omitted (an explicit empty list is refused, and asking for a permission you lack is an error). site_ids takes public site ids (pa_...) and restricts the token to those sites, and when empty the token works for every site its member can access (or keeps the site list of the token making this call). expires_at is optional ISO 8601 and must be in the future and at most 3 years away, omit it for a token that never expires. allowed_ips limits the token to those IPs or CIDR ranges. A token making this call needs tokens.manage. A workspace that requires two-factor authentication refuses tokens for members without a second factor of their own. Returns the same fields as api_tokens_list plus token.

item.name: List API tokens

request.name: List API tokens

description.content: Lists the API tokens of a workspace, newest first and paginated. Without the tokens.manage permission you only see your own tokens, with it you see every member's. Revoked and expired tokens are hidden unless include_revoked is true. Each item has id (uuid, used by api_tokens_delete), name, token_prefix (the first characters, for recognizing a token), owner (the member's email), permissions (names such as analytics.read), site_ids (public site ids pa_..., an empty array means every site the owner can access), allowed_ips, oauth_client (the connected app's name when the token was issued through OAuth, otherwise null), status (active, expired or revoked), expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at and created_at. The secret itself is never returned here, token is always null in a list. It is only shown once by api_tokens_create.

item.name: Revoke an API token

request.name: Revoke an API token

description.content: Revokes an API token immediately and permanently. Requests that use it fail from then on, and a revoked token cannot be restored, create a new one instead. The token record stays in the list with status revoked (use api_tokens_list with include_revoked to see it), and revoking an already revoked token changes nothing. Take the id (a uuid) from api_tokens_list. You can revoke your own tokens, revoking someone else's needs tokens.manage and reach over every site the token covers. A token calling this needs tokens.manage. Returns the revoked token without its secret.

request.name: Get your profile and preferences

description.content: Returns the signed-in member's own profile and preferences. Use it to read settings before changing them with account_update. This is about the person, not a workspace. Workspace plan and invoices are under billing_get. Fields are email, unconfirmed_email (set while an email change awaits confirmation, otherwise null), name (nullable), theme (system, light or dark), default_landing (sites or last_site), locale (language code for the signed-in app), timezone (IANA name, nullable), shortcuts_enabled, reduce_motion, product_emails, site_audit_emails, marketing_emails, newsletter (all booleans where true means subscribed), two_factor (boolean), passkeys (count of registered passkeys) and created_at (ISO 8601). item.name: Update your profile and preferences

request.name: Update your profile and preferences

description.content: Updates the signed-in member's own profile, display preferences and email subscriptions. Only the inputs you send change, everything else stays as it is. Changing email does not take effect at once. A confirmation email is sent to the new address (rate limited) and unconfirmed_email shows the pending address until it is confirmed. API tokens cannot change the email address and cannot turn marketing_emails back on after an unsubscribe, both need a signed-in browser. Turning marketing_emails off is allowed. Sessions opened by a workspace identity provider may only change the display settings (theme, default_landing, locale, timezone, shortcuts_enabled, reduce_motion). Returns the updated account in the same shape as account_get. This does not delete the account and cannot change workspace settings.

item.name: Create an alert

request.name: Create an alert

description.content: Creates an alert rule that watches a site (or the whole workspace for kind usage) and notifies the chosen channels when it triggers. Path takes workspace_id. name and kind are required. kind decides what else is needed. threshold needs site_id, metric (visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce_rate or conversion), operator (gt, gte, lt or lte) and threshold, and conversion also needs goal_id. anomaly needs site_id and metric (visitors, visits or pageviews), compares the last window with the same window in each of the previous 4 weeks and uses sensitivity (low, medium or high). operator lt only alerts on drops, gt only on spikes and empty on both. goal needs site_id, goal_id and threshold (completions in the window). no_data needs site_id and threshold in hours without events (default 24). usage needs no site and threshold as percent of the monthly event allowance (default 80). uptime needs site_id and optionally uptime_check_id (default all checks of the site). ssl needs site_id and threshold in days before a certificate or domain expires (default 14). vitals needs site_id, metric (lcp, inp, cls, fcp or ttfb) and threshold in milliseconds (a score for cls). subscriptions needs site_id, metric (mrr_drop: MRR fell by more than threshold percent in the last 30 days, churn_rate or mrr_churn_rate: churn over the last 30 days is above threshold percent) and threshold (default 10), and skips while the site has no payment provider connected or nothing to measure. window_minutes (default 60, 5 to 10080) is how far back each evaluation looks. channel_ids come from notification_channels_list and sensitivity defaults to medium. Alerts are evaluated automatically every 5 minutes. bounce_rate and conversion thresholds are percents from 0 to 100. testimonials needs site_id and metric, which says what it watches: new (a new testimonial arrives), low_rating (a rating of 3 or lower arrives), approved (a testimonial is approved), allowance (the month's allowance of new testimonials is 80% used, used up, or holding a testimonial as waiting), sync_found (a sync finds new reviews), import_failed (an import fails, or a source fails three syncs in a row), removal_requested (someone asks for their testimonial to be removed) or request_bounced (a request email bounces). A testimonials alert is not evaluated every 5 minutes: it triggers at once each time the thing happens, records an incident that is already resolved, and its state stays ok. With metric allowance it watches the whole workspace and keeps no site. Returns the created alert with state ok.

item.name: Funnels
Create a funnel

request.name: Create a funnel

description.content: Creates a funnel, a sequence of steps that visits move through, measured per visit. Pass name and steps, an ordered list of {type, value, match, name}. type is page, event or goal. value is a path for page steps (for example /pricing), a custom event name for event steps, or a goal id (goal_..., from goals_list) for goal steps. match is only for page steps and is exact, prefix, glob (* wildcard) or regex, defaulting to glob when the value has a * and exact otherwise. name is an optional label. Steps with an empty value are dropped. order_mode is strict (each step must come after the previous one, the default) or any (steps in any order). window is visit (the default) or day, and both measure within a single visit because no visitor id is stored. Plan limits apply. Free allows 3 funnels per site and 5 steps, Pro allows 10 steps and Business 20, and a funnel needs at least 2 steps. Returns the funnel with id (fun_...). Read results with funnels_get. Needs the content.write permission.

item.name: Group the free-text answers to one question into themes (Business plan)

request.name: Group the free-text answers to one question into themes (Business plan)

description.content: Uses AI to group the written answers to one free-text question into themes. Business plan only. Choose it after surveys_get shows a text question with enough answers, and pass question_key (the key of a question of kind text from surveys_get). It needs at least 5 written answers and uses the 300 most recent. The result lists up to 12 themes, each with label, count, sentiment (positive, neutral or negative) and example (a representative answer, may be null), plus answers (how many answers were summarized) and generated_at. Each new generation uses one question from the workspace's monthly AI allowance, which is given back if it fails. The result is cached against the answers, so calling again with no new answers costs nothing. It fails with a validation error when the plan does not include it, the allowance is used up, the AI is not configured or there are too few answers.

item.name: Warehouse sync
Add a warehouse destination

request.name: Add a warehouse destination

description.content: Adds a warehouse destination that receives each day's raw events (Business plan only). Daily at 02:00 UTC the previous UTC day is uploaded, the first run is at the next 02:00 UTC, and a failed run is retried an hour later. kind must be given and decides the required settings. s3 (also GCS, R2 and MinIO through endpoint) needs bucket, access_key_id and secret_access_key, with optional region, prefix and endpoint (https, public hosts only). bigquery needs service_account_json, dataset and table, with optional project_id. snowflake needs account, user, private_key (PEM RSA), database, schema and table, with optional warehouse and role. azure needs sas_url (an https blob container SAS link with write permission), with optional prefix. Secrets (secret_access_key, service_account_json, private_key, sas_url) are write only and are never returned. site_ids limits the sites (pa_... ids), empty means every site, and a member or token limited to some sites must name them. Event properties are only sent when marked safe to export (see event_properties_list). Needs the workspace.manage permission. Returns the destination with id (whd_...), a masked target and configured (the names of the filled in settings).

item.name: Estimate traffic missed by consent-based analytics

request.name: Estimate traffic missed by consent-based analytics

description.content: Free calculator that estimates how much traffic a cookie-consent analytics tool misses compared with cookieless tracking. It is a simple model, not a measurement. Inputs are monthly_visitors (a whole number above 0), consent_rate (percent of visitors who accept the banner, 0 to 100) and adblock_share (percent whose blockers stop the script, 0 to 100, default 25). Returns the inputs plus measured_with_consent (visitors the consent tool sees), missed (visitors it does not see), missed_percent (one decimal), measured_cookieless (visitors reachable without a banner) and recovered_by_cookieless (visitors gained over consent tracking). All visitor counts are whole numbers. It makes no requests and uses no account data. Public, no authentication needed.

item.name: Check a page’s Referrer-Policy and CSP for analytics

request.name: Check a page’s Referrer-Policy and CSP for analytics

description.content: Fetches one public page and checks the response headers that affect analytics. Use it when tracking data is missing or referrers look wrong. It looks at Referrer-Policy, the Content-Security-Policy script-src and connect-src directives (whether Privatus Analytics may load and send data), Permissions-Policy and the number of Set-Cookie headers. Returns url (the final URL after up to 3 redirects), status (HTTP status) and findings, each with check, value (nullable), level (ok, warn or info) and a plain-language note. The URL must be http or https and public, private and internal addresses are refused, only the first 1 MB is read and the fetch times out after 5 seconds. Rate limited to 10 calls a minute per client. Public, no authentication needed.

item.name: List cookies and known trackers on a page

request.name: List cookies and known trackers on a page

description.content: Fetches one public page and lists the cookies it sets and the known third-party trackers it references. Use it for a quick check of what a page loads before choosing a consent approach. It is a static scan of the HTML and response headers only, it does not run JavaScript, so cookies set by scripts and tags loaded later by a tag manager are missed. Returns url (final URL after up to 3 redirects), status, truncated (true when only the first 1 MB was read), cookies (name, domain, path, expires, secure, http_only and same_site, values are never returned), trackers (name, category, match and evidence, where category is advertising, analytics, session_recording, tag_manager, marketing or privacy_analytics) and third_party_hosts (sorted host names of other sites). The URL must be public http or https, with a 5 second fetch timeout, and calls are limited to 10 a minute per client. Public, no authentication needed.

item.name: Update workspace security settings (2FA, login methods, session lifetime, IP allowlist, support access)

request.name: Update workspace security settings (2FA, login methods, session lifetime, IP allowlist, support access)

description.content: Changes the workspace security policy, only the inputs you send. enforce_2fa true requires every member to use two-factor authentication and needs the Business plan. login_methods replaces the allowed list with values from password, magic_link, passkey, google, github, apple and sso, and removing a method signs out members' remembered logins so they must log in again. session_ttl_hours signs members out after that many hours (0 removes the limit). app_ip_allowlist replaces the list of IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to reach the app and API (Business plan, an empty list means anywhere) and is refused if it would exclude the IP of the caller, so you cannot lock yourself out. support_access true lets Privatus Analytics support view the workspace for 7 days and false withdraws that access. Requires workspace.manage. Returns the policy (see workspace_security_get).

description.content: Changes a workspace's name, default timezone, default currency or whether it takes part in benchmarks, only the inputs you send. timezone is an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin and currency is a 3-letter ISO 4217 code. These are defaults for new sites, they do not change existing sites (use sites_update for those). Requires workspace.manage. Returns the workspace (see workspaces_get).

info.name: Privatus Analytics API
info.description:
The full REST API of [Privatus Analytics](https://privatusanalytics.com), the privacy-first, cookieless web analytics platform.

Read stats (aggregate, time series, breakdowns, live visitors), manage sites, goals, funnels, segments, alerts, uptime checks, status pages, experiments, exports and testimonials, and subscribe to signed webhooks.

## Get started

1. In Privatus Analytics, open **Workspace settings → API tokens** and create a token (`pat_...`).
2. Fork this collection and set the `token` variable to it.
3. Run **Get started → List workspaces**, then **List sites**. Copy a site ID (`pa_...`) into the `site_id` variable.
4. Run **Get started → Visitors in the last 7 days**.

A token works in one workspace. JSON responses are `{ "data": ..., "meta": ... }` and errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`.

Docs: [privatusanalytics.com/docs/api](https://privatusanalytics.com/docs/api). OpenAPI: [privatusanalytics.com/openapi.json](https://privatusanalytics.com/openapi.json). Support: hello@privatusanalytics.com.
